items.statement:
Let $D^2$ be the oriented closed disk and let $K\subset S^3=\partial B^4$ be a smooth oriented knot, meaning the image of an orientation-preserving smooth embedding of a circle. A **ribbon immersion** for $K$ is a smooth immersion $f:D^2\to S^3$ whose boundary restriction is an embedding onto $K$ and whose only multiple points form finitely many pairwise disjoint transverse double arcs $\gamma_1,\ldots,\gamma_m$. For each $i$, the full preimage of $\gamma_i$ consists of two disjoint embedded arcs $\alpha_i$ and $\beta_i$ in $D^2$: $\alpha_i$ is properly embedded, with its two endpoints on $\partial D^2$ and its interior in $\operatorname{Int}D^2$, while $\beta_i$ is compact and lies in $\operatorname{Int}D^2$. There are no triple points or other self-intersections. A **ribbon disk** for $K$ is such a ribbon immersion, and $K$ is a **ribbon knot** if it admits a ribbon disk.

A **band** on a link in $S^3$ is the image of a smoothly embedded rectangle whose two opposite attaching edges lie on the link and whose remaining points are disjoint from it. A **band move** removes the attaching edges, inserts the other two edges, and rounds the corners; the embedded band, including its half-twist data, is part of the move. A **no-maximum disk movie** is the family of regular level links of a smooth proper disk $D\subset B^4$ for which the squared radial function $\rho(x)=\lVert x\rVert^2$ is Morse in the disk interior and has only index-$0$ minima and index-$1$ saddles. A minimum creates a split unknot and a saddle performs an oriented band move; there are no maxima. The no-maximum disk movie is a second presentation convention used by the design for explicit ribbon examples. This movie model and the ribbon-immersion definition above describe the same class of knots: a finite birth-and-band induction converts the movie to an immersion, and cutting the proper double-arc preimages converts an immersion to a disk-and-band movie. The local resolution lemma proves only that a ribbon immersion pushes rel boundary to a smooth proper disk in $B^4$. The slice-ribbon conjecture asks whether every smooth slice knot admits a ribbon immersion as defined above.
items.axiom_use: ACω is retained for the library's slice-genus convention; the ribbon-singularity definition itself is choice-free.

items.statement: Let $f:D^2\to S^3$ be a smooth immersion of an oriented disk whose boundary is an embedded oriented knot $K$. Suppose that its only self-intersections are finitely many pairwise disjoint transverse double arcs, and that the two preimage arcs of each double arc are one properly embedded arc in $D^2$ and one compact arc contained in $\operatorname{Int}D^2$. Then there is a smooth proper embedding $\widetilde f:(D^2,\partial D^2)\to(B^4,S^3)$ with $\widetilde f|_{\partial D^2}=f|_{\partial D^2}$.
items.axiom_use: The finite local construction is choice-free; the declared ACω dependency is retained from the approved slice-genus interface.

items.statement: For every smooth oriented knot $K\subset S^3$ that bounds a smooth properly embedded disk in $B^4$, must there also exist a smooth immersion $f:D^2\to S^3$ whose boundary is $K$ and whose only self-intersections are finitely many transverse double arcs, each with one properly embedded preimage arc and one preimage arc contained in the interior of $D^2$?

items.title: A reverse-mirror sum admits an explicit ribbon immersion

references.title: Arunima Ray, Slice Knots and Knot Concordance
references.locator: Propositions 1.5 and 1.6, PDF p.3; ribbon singularity in Figure 6, PDF p.5. The explicit strip proof is supplied here.

items.statement: Assume the Axiom of Countable Choice. Every smooth oriented knot $K$ in the standard oriented three-sphere has its connected sum with its reverse mirror represented by the boundary of a smooth immersed disk in $S^3$ whose only multiple points are finitely many transverse double arcs, each having one proper preimage arc and one interior preimage arc. Consequently $K\#K^\dagger$ is ribbon in the ribbon-immersion sense.

items.statement: Assume the Axiom of Countable Choice. For a smooth oriented knot $K\subset S^3$, the following are equivalent: $K$ bounds a ribbon immersion of a disk in $S^3$; and $K$ bounds a smooth properly embedded disk in the standard four-ball for which squared radial distance is Morse in the interior with only critical points of indices zero and one. In the second presentation the disk has product collars at its boundary.

items.statement: Assume the Axiom of Countable Choice. Every smooth oriented knot $K\subset S^3$ that bounds a smooth immersed disk in $S^3$ with only ribbon double arcs bounds a smooth properly embedded disk in $B^4$ with boundary $K$. In particular, its smooth slice genus is zero.
items.axiom_use: ACω is the explicit background assumption of the library's smooth slice-genus convention. The local geometric resolution uses no choice.

items.statement: Assume ACω. Let $T$ be the standard right-handed trefoil, represented by the closure of the standard two-strand braid with three positive half-twists, and let $T^\dagger$ be its reverse mirror. Choose the connected-sum balls on arcs colored $0$ in the Fox 3-colorings described below. The square knot $T\#T^\dagger$ is nontrivial, is ribbon, and bounds a smooth properly embedded disk in $B^4$.
items.axiom_use: ACω is used through the ribbon-disk construction and Reidemeister equivalence; the finite Fox-coloring calculation and local move bijections are choice-free.
